entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Donatus of Zadar was a Dalmatian saint and diplomat who became bishop of the Dalmatian city-state of Zadar (Zara) in the 8th century CE. Born into a noble family, Donatus rose to prominence through his piety and political acumen, eventually earning the respect of the Byzantine Emperor and the Catholic Church. His diplomatic efforts helped maintain peace between the Byzantine and Lombard kingdoms, securing a crucial alliance that would shape the fate of the region for centuries to come. Donatus's legacy extends beyond his own lifetime, as his policies and legacy influenced the development of the Croatian Kingdom and the modern-day city of Zadar. His feast day is celebrated on 25 February, and he remains a revered figure in Dalmatian history and Catholic tradition.
